name: Fashion ontology for the multimodal AI knowledge graph sample
comment: Category and attribute vocabulary reused from the Fashionpedia ontology (CC BY 4.0, https://fashionpedia.github.io/home/data_license.html). Changes made for this sample: the flat catalog is expressed in OWL 2 (groups and categories as classes, attribute families as classes with attribute values as named individuals, one has<Family> object property per family), an applicability matrix is added as property domains, hasPart links garments to parts/closures/decorations, four jewelry categories that Fashionpedia does not have (earring, necklace, bracelet, ring) are added to the group of other accessories, each marked with a skos:editorialNote, a brand knowledge-graph schema (Look, Item, Statement, Article, Line, Brand) is added, and a closed vocabulary of occasions (the class Occasion, nine named individuals and the property for from Look to Occasion) is added, each term marked with a skos:editorialNote. No Fashionpedia image or annotation is included.

nodes.label: Apparel
nodes.comment: A wearable garment or accessory (the Fashionpedia main apparel categories and the jewelry this sample adds).

nodes.label: Article
nodes.comment: An editorial source document: magazine feature, brand blog post, lookbook text.

nodes.label: Attribute value
nodes.comment: A fine-grained apparel attribute; each family is a subclass and each value a named individual.

nodes.label: bracelet
nodes.comment: Jewelry worn around the wrist, such as chain bracelets, bangles and cuffs.

nodes.label: Brand
nodes.comment: A brand (the fictional 'Velloway' in the sample data).

nodes.label: earring
nodes.comment: Jewelry worn on the ear, such as studs, hoops, drop and chandelier earrings.

nodes.label: Garment component
nodes.comment: A part, closure or decoration of a garment (Fashionpedia apparel parts).

nodes.label: Item
nodes.comment: A concrete catalog product; its category is one of the Apparel classes.

nodes.label: Line
nodes.comment: A brand's product line or collection.

nodes.label: Look
nodes.comment: A styled outfit: an ordered set of items shown together (lookbook, campaign, editorial).

nodes.label: necklace
nodes.comment: Jewelry worn around the neck, such as chains, pendants, chokers and strands of pearls or beads.

nodes.label: Occasion
nodes.comment: What a look is worn for.

nodes.label: ring
nodes.comment: Jewelry worn on a finger, such as bands, cocktail and signet rings.

nodes.label: Statement
nodes.comment: A single editorial claim extracted from an article (e.g. a styling rule or trend note).

nodes.label: Dress
nodes.definition: A day look built around a dress.

nodes.label: Evening
nodes.definition: An evening out: dinner, drinks, a show.

nodes.label: Smart casual
nodes.definition: Casual pieces dressed up a step.

nodes.label: contains
nodes.comment: A look contains an item.

nodes.label: for
nodes.comment: The occasion a look is worn for.

nodes.label: has attribute
nodes.comment: Generic link from a garment to one of its attribute values; sub-properties are one per family.

nodes.label: has part
nodes.comment: A garment part, closure or decoration visible on the garment.

nodes.label: illustrates
nodes.comment: What an editorial statement is about.

nodes.label: is category
nodes.comment: The apparel category of an item.

nodes.label: layered with
nodes.comment: Two items worn layered in the same look.

nodes.label: pairs with
nodes.comment: Category-level styling rule: garments of these categories are recommended together.
